title: Examination of the significance of a video to improve the medical education before cardiac imaging procedure.
summary: A video is shown to patients as an additional information tool when explaining the procedure to patients prior to radiological imaging of the heart, which is intended to improve understanding of the examination and reduce patient anxiety. In order to evaluate the possible benefit of the video, some patients were randomly shown a simpler, additional comparison video or received only the standard physician consultation without an additional video. Patient anxiety was then evaluated using a questionnaire and the image data from the radiological examination was analyzed with regard to image quality.

interventions.name: Group Nr.1 receives a detailed video-assisted consent including a detailed video, written and verbal consent. They undergo a questionnaire-based testing of anxiety and satisfaction. In addition, artefacts of the radiological images will be evaluated.

Group Nr.2 receives a basic video-assisted consent including a simple video, written and verbal consent. They undergo a questionnaire-based testing of anxiety and satisfaction. In addition, artefacts of the radiological images will be evaluated.
Group Nr.3 receives only written and verbal consent. They undergo a questionnaire-based testing of anxiety and satisfaction. In addition, artefacts of the radiological images will be evaluated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients undergoing cardiac CT before transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), cardiac CT to exclude coronary heart disease (CHC), cardiac MRI to exclude myocarditis or ischemic cardiomyopathy or other cardiac MRI
- all participants have to be capable of giving consent and have to voluntarily agree to participate in the trial
- speak German fluently
Exclusion criteria:
- Panic attacs or anxiety disorders in medical history
- Cognitive disability (Dementia, psychosis etc.)
- Currently recieving anxiolytical medication
- Significant visual or hearing impairment
